subject: Post-call: Concurrency & rate limits follow-up (Acme Analytics)
messages:
From: Samir Patel <samir@acme.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 25 Jun 2027 16:10:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up: concurrency / latency targets (post-demo)

Thanks for the demo today — really helpful overview of Redwood's runtime and routing options. Quick recap from our side and a few clarification questions so we can align on next steps:

- Business context: we plan to roll out a new assistant across our Analytics product in Q4. The initial region is US.
- Expected traffic profile (rough): steady-state ~250 QPS, average request size ~350 tokens, peak day expected bursts up to ~600 concurrent requests during promotions.
- Latency SLO: target p95 generation latency <= 200ms for up to 1024-token responses (this is critical for our interactive workflows).
- Streaming: ~60% of requests will use streaming responses (progressive chunks), average stream duration ~400ms.
- Connection behavior: clients will multiplex up to 16 HTTP/1.1 keep-alive connections from our edge pool; we'll likely use connection pooling and HTTP keep-alive.

Questions:
1) For the numbers above — are those concurrency figures (parallel request count) acceptable for Redwood hosted or do you recommend Dedicated?
2) What rate limits / quota baseline should we request to avoid 429s during launches? Any guidance on burst-to-sustained ratios?
3) Any specific connection pooling settings or HTTP client recommendations to avoid head-of-line or connection exhaustion issues?

Attachments: acme-slo-requirements.pdf (SLO doc we mentioned)

Next steps: can you share a proposed quota plan and whether we should plan a Dedicated pilot? We'll also need a contact for procurement (I'll include Nina's email in follow-up).

Thanks,
Samir
Director of Platform
Acme Analytics
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Patel <samir@acme.ai>
Cc: Logan Wright <logan@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 25 Jun 2027 16:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: concurrency / latency targets (post-demo)

Hi Samir — great to chat earlier. Thanks for the clear recap and the attached SLO doc. High-level responses below, plus a couple clarifying Qs so we size quota appropriately.

Summary responses:
- Hosted vs Dedicated: Your steady-state of ~250 QPS with 600-concurrency peak is on the edge for hosted; we frequently support similar volumes, but to guarantee p95 <= 200ms at 1024 tokens and to give you a predictable SLA during launches we recommend evaluating Redwood Dedicated (reserved GPU capacity) coupled with our Smart Routing for cost control.
- Initial quota guidance: propose a baseline concurrency quota of 200 concurrent requests with a burst allowance to 800 during ramp events. We'll also propose a rate cap (requests/min) to protect shared pools; details below.
- Streaming/keep-alive: streaming is supported and performs well on our runtime. We recommend HTTP/1.1 keep-alive with 8-16 connections per edge instance and client-side request queuing rather than creating many short-lived connections. For streaming we expose chunked transfer encoding and advise using libraries that support backpressure (e.g., netty/grpc-web patterns).

Clarifying Qs:
- When you say peak "600 concurrent requests" — is that concurrent open connections actively generating tokens, or queued requests waiting on slots?
- For streaming percent (~60%), what's the average token output size per stream and typical # of chunks (rough estimate)?

Next steps (proposed):
1) We'll draft an initial quota proposal and share it with infra (looping Logan).
2) If you want a hard p95 guarantee for 1024 tokens we should scope a Dedicated pilot (2-4 weeks) to validate under your traffic shape.
3) I'll ask procurement contact (Nina) for PO flow once we agree on the quota/price.

Attaching: redwood-initial-quota-proposal.pdf (strawman)

Best,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
From: Logan Wright <logan@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 27 Jun 2027 10:12:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Follow-up: concurrency: latency targets (post-demo)

Marissa — looping in recommended quota numbers and engineering notes for Samir. These are our starting points; we can tighten them after the pilot load tests.

Proposal (initial):
- Baseline concurrency quota: 200 concurrent requests (guaranteed capacity on host).
- Burst capacity: allow up to 800 concurrent requests with degraded routing to Dedicated when contention > baseline. Burst window: 30 minutes rolling.
- Rate limits: soft-limit 15,000 requests/min (250 rps sustained), hard-limit 30,000 requests/min (500 rps sustained) for initial period.
- Token throughput: allocate token budget to support average response sizes of 350 tokens at 250 QPS (we'll provision token TPS accordingly).
- Streaming: keep streaming connections open; recommend max concurrent streams per client 100 — we'll enforce per-connection limits server-side to avoid slow-sink issues.

Engineering notes:
- To hit p95 <= 200ms for 1024 tokens, we should target Dedicated nodes with optimized kernels (FP16/quant profiles) and pinned model variants. If you cannot go Dedicated immediately, we can still optimize on Hosted via traffic shaping and KV-prefix caching but there will be some variability during multi-tenant contention.
- Connection pooling: recommend long-lived connections, 8-16 connections per edge pool, HTTP keep-alive, and client-side retry with exponential backoff for 429s.

I'll assign an infra engineer to the pilot once Samir confirms — need a contact and preferred pilot window.

— Logan
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

Thanks Marissa/Logan — this is helpful and inline with our expectations. A few quick items to confirm so we can move procurement forward:

- We confirm that the 600 number refers to active concurrent token-generation requests during peak promos (not queued).
- We agree to the proposed baseline/burst numbers as a starting point: baseline 200, burst 800. Please put this into a formal quote so procurement can review.
- Procurement contact: Nina Gomez (nina.gomez@acme.ai). She may reach out for contract/PO templates and vendor info.
- Can Redwood commit to a p95 <= 200ms SLA for streaming up to 1024 tokens under the Dedicated pilot? If not a hard SLA, please specify expected variance and fallback behavior (automatic routing to smaller model variant / degrade to non-streaming).

Attachments: acme-procurement.pdf (procurement contact + PO info)

If you can send a formal quote and proposed pilot window (we prefer Jul 18-Aug 1), we'll get procurement engaged.

Thanks,
Samir
Director of Platform
Acme Analytics
